title: Two Pointers
description: Move one or more indices through the array to avoid nested scans.
identify: The problem asks for in-place rearrangement or compaction.
The array is sorted, partially partitioned, or can be scanned from both ends.
You can make progress by moving only the pointer that violates the target condition.
Relative order or partition boundaries matter more than random access.
explanation: Two pointers reduce repeated work by turning a nested search or extra-array operation into a single pass. One pointer usually scans the input while another marks the next write position, boundary, or matching index.

title: Prefix Sum
description: Store cumulative values to convert subarray questions into differences of earlier states.
identify: The question is about a contiguous subarray or range.
A range value can be expressed as prefix[right] - prefix[left - 1].
Negative numbers prevent a normal sliding window.
You need to count or find previous cumulative states quickly.
explanation: Prefix sums remember the value of everything seen so far. If the current prefix is P and an earlier prefix was P - K, the subarray between those two positions has sum K. Hashing makes this lookup constant time.

title: Kadane's
description: Track the best subarray ending at the current index and update the global answer.
identify: The problem asks for a maximum or minimum contiguous subarray value.
At each index you choose between extending the previous subarray or starting fresh.
A bad running contribution should be dropped.
Only local running state is needed.
explanation: Kadane's algorithm keeps the best subarray that must end at the current element. If extending the old subarray is worse than starting at the current value, reset the running sum.

title: Matrix
description: Use boundaries, coordinates, and row/column relationships to traverse grids cleanly.
identify: The input is a 2D grid or triangular arrangement.
The traversal direction or boundary changes after each pass.
Rows and columns carry independent meaning.
You need careful index limits to avoid duplicate visits.
explanation: Matrix problems become easier when you name the moving boundaries or the coordinate relationship. The goal is to make each cell's visit rule explicit and guard against revisiting cells.

title: Observation Based
description: Exploit a small mathematical or logical property instead of applying a heavy data structure.
identify: The main trick is a property of the values or operation.
A single scan can maintain the required best answer.
The problem looks simple but has edge cases around order or wraparound.
Sorting or hashing would work but is more than needed.
explanation: Observation based problems usually depend on one invariant: minimum price so far, current streak length, or how rotation changes positions. Once the invariant is clear, the implementation is often a compact linear scan.
